literature_notes: NEO1 (Neogenin) is a Type I single-pass transmembrane protein with an extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 34 onward) and an intracellular C-terminus (residue 1461). Every ledger clip that specifies tag position (L1–L6) places a FLAG/MYC or 6×Myc epitope at the C-terminus, which is intracellular (residues 1127–1461). These are recorded in other_positions. L7 ('FLAG-tagged full-length mouse NEO1') names no residue and the tag position is unstated — it cannot be pinned and is disqualified under the commercial-plasmid/unstated-position rule. L8 and L9 describe a 'NEO1-mVenus' fusion; the naming convention (protein-FP hyphenation) indicates a C-terminal fusion, again intracellular. No ledger line grounds an insertion on the extracellular face at any pinnable residue or named loop. Zero extracellular surface sites qualify.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG/MYC epitope on full-length mouse Neo1 (fNeo1); function preserved (hepcidin induction unaffected), but the C-terminus of this Type I TM protein is intracellular (residues 1127–1461), so the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
C-terminal 6×Myc epitope on full-length mouse Neogenin expressed in neurons; C-terminus is intracellular in this Type I TM protein.
NEO1-mVenus fusion expressed in COS-7 cells; 'NEO1-mVenus' naming indicates C-terminal fluorescent protein fusion, which is intracellular given the Type I topology of NEO1.
